last.name: The operation carried out last
last.text: Evaluate expressions using the order of operations

common.name: Taking a common factor out
common.text: Factor out the greatest common factor

questions.stem: Six can be written `3 + 3`, and it can be written `2 * 3`. Which of the two is written as a product?

opts.d: `3 + 3` is two numbers added.
Both come to 6. The question is which one is written as a multiplication.

work.why: Both are 6. One is written as an addition and the other as a multiplication.

aspects.body: The same happens with letters. `x + x` and `2x` are the same amount, one written as a sum and one as a product.

questions.stem: Work out `2 * 3 + 4`. Which operation do you carry out last?

opts.d: The multiplying is done first, on the 2 and the 3. The 4 is added to the 6 that gives.

opts.t: Either one, depending on where you start
opts.d: Order of operations fixes it: the multiplying is done before the adding.

work.why: The multiplying happens first and the adding happens to its result.

questions.stem: Work out `2 * (3 + 4)`. Which operation do you carry out last?

opts.d: The bracket is worked out first and gives 7. The 2 then multiplies that 7.

opts.t: There is only one operation here
opts.d: There are two: an addition inside the bracket and a multiplication outside it.

work.why: `2 * 3 + 4` comes to 10 and `2 * (3 + 4)` comes to 14. The same three numbers, and the operation carried out last is what separates them.

aspects.body: Whatever is carried out last is what the whole expression is. `2 * 3 + 4` finishes with an addition, so it is a sum. `2 * (3 + 4)` finishes with a multiplication, so it is a product. With numbers this can be settled by working it out. With letters there is nothing to work out, and it has to be read off the writing instead.

sets.name: The sign that is not there

opts.t: A sum, and `x` and 2 share no factor

opts.d: `x` and 2 are added here. `2x` would be the product.

opts.t: A sum that can be written as a product
opts.d: `x` and 2 share no factor, so there is nothing to take out front.

work.why: Not every expression can be written as a product. This one has nothing common to take out.

opts.t: Nowhere. Two brackets written side by side are multiplied

opts.d: The `+` inside the first bracket adds `x` and 2.

opts.t: There is no multiplication in this expression
opts.d: Brackets written next to each other with nothing between them are multiplied.

work.why: Multiplication between brackets is written by leaving the space empty.

aspects.body: Every other operation here has a symbol you can point at. The multiplication is the one with nothing to point at.

questions.stem: Put `x` = 3 into `(x+2)+(x-3)` and into `(x+2)(x-3)`. What does each come to?

opts.d: The second is `5 * 0`, which is 0.
The first is `5 + 0`, which is 5.

work.why: The two expressions differ by one character and come to different numbers.

opts.t: One of the two brackets is 0, and anything multiplied by 0 is 0

opts.d: `x + 2` comes to 5 when `x` is 3.
5 and 0 added come to 5. These two brackets are multiplied.

work.why: A product is 0 when one of the things being multiplied is 0.

opts.d: The `+ 3` sits outside the bracket. The 2 multiplies `(x+2)` and nothing else.

opts.t: A product, since it contains a multiplication
opts.d: It contains a multiplication. What the `+` separates is `2(x+2)` and 3, and those are added.

work.why: The `+` separates `2(x+2)` from 3. The 2 multiplies only the bracket beside it.

questions.stem: Which of these is written as a product?

opts.d: This one finishes with an addition.
This one finishes with a subtraction.
This one finishes with an addition.

work.why: Three of the four contain a multiplication. Only one of them is a multiplication.

aspects.body: `x(x+1) - 3(x+1)` has `(x+1)` in both parts, so `(x+1)` can be written once out front. That step is what the other review works on.

sets.name: Which operation, and then doing it

questions.stem: `(x+2) + (x-3)`. Compute. Which operation does the writing ask for?

opts.d: The `+` between the brackets adds them.

opts.t: Nothing, it is already as short as it goes
opts.d: The two `x` terms can be collected, and 2 and `-3` can be combined.

work.why: The sign between the brackets says which operation to carry out.

opts.d: 2 and `-3` come to `-1`.
The two `x` terms are added, giving `2x`. They are not multiplied.
The 3 multiplies both terms inside the bracket, the 2 as well as the `x`.
The 3 multiplies the `x` as well.

work.why: The 3 multiplies each term inside the bracket.

questions.stem: `(x+2)(x-3)`. Compute. Which operation does the writing ask for?

opts.d: Nothing is written between the brackets, and that empty space is a multiplication.

opts.t: Subtracting the second bracket from the first
opts.d: The `-` sits inside the second bracket, between `x` and 3.

work.why: The two brackets are written side by side, and nothing between them means multiply.

opts.d: Each term in the first bracket multiplies each term in the second: `x * x`, `x * (-3)`, `2 * x`, `2 * (-3)`.
`-3x` and `2x` come to `-x`.

work.why: `x * x` is `x^2`, then `-3x` and `2x` give `-x`, and `2 * (-3)` gives `-6`.
